identity.title: [v0.92.1][GCP-D1] Deploy the bounded private foundation and prove non-GPU workload disposal

values.summary: After recovering stale #731 review/publication truth for PR #739, the current follow-up remediation tightened the live GCP scripts and added no-live behavioral guard evidence for the review blockers. Mutation authorization fails closed on expired deadlines, approvals older than 120 minutes, cleanup windows over 30 minutes, and non-service-account impersonation identities. The disposable workload script now reads the authorized impersonated identity from the packet, routes live create/delete/readback/storage/cleanup gcloud calls through that service account, arms cleanup before the create attempt, uses an EXIT cleanup trap plus independent authorized deadline reaper, proves guest readiness/metadata identity, enumerates expanded zero-residue surfaces including forwarding rules, firewall overrides, VM-specific IAM, Terraform state run labels, and storage objects/all versions, and fails closed on injected post-create, partial-create, and storage-residue cases. The foundation apply script now uses service-account impersonation both for Terraform access-token provisioning and for live gcloud readbacks of project/subnet/firewall/OS Login/IAM/bucket/logging state, with rollback-on-failure. No new live GCP mutation was run during this remediation; earlier retained live foundation/workload evidence remains historical evidence only, and any fresh live rerun requires a new unexpired operator authorization packet.
actual_changes: Recovered #731 from the stale PR #739 review/publication state before editing, and later recovered the fresh follow-up review assignment after reviewer fresh-session:b46c30c4-d885-4795-86e3-38a06bf88160 returned P1/P2 findings.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-authorization-packet.sh to require an unexpired cleanup deadline, approved_at_utc when approved, approval age no greater than 120 minutes, cleanup lifetime no greater than 30 minutes, and a service-account impersonation identity.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-disposable-workload-proof.sh to validate authorization before mutation, read the authorized impersonated service account from the packet, route live gcloud create/delete/readback/storage/cleanup commands through --impersonate-service-account, arm cleanup before the VM create attempt, arm an independent authorized deadline reaper, trap failures with cleanup deletion, prove guest readiness and metadata service-account identity, enumerate storage objects/all versions from the accepted foundation buckets, and check forwarding rules, firewall overrides, VM-specific IAM, storage-object, and Terraform-state run-label residue in addition to instances, disks, and addresses.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-foundation-apply-and-readback.sh to obtain Terraform access through an impersonated service-account token, use the same authorized identity for live gcloud readbacks, trap failed apply/readback with terraform destroy rollback, and assert exact project metadata, workload service account, firewall denominator, IAM, bucket labels, and logging metric readbacks.

Expanded .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-remediation-guards.sh with retained .csdlc/evidence/731/remediation-guards/** proving the new guards without live GCP mutation, including synthetic rejected packets, success-path workload readiness/residue execution, storage-residue rejection, partial-create cleanup, injected post-create cleanup, foundation readback success, injected foundation rollback, and fail-closed mock enforcement that every live gcloud command is invoked with the authorized impersonated service account.
Stabilized traced mock evidence by normalizing background deadline reaper PIDs so rerun proof is deterministic.
Preserved the historical live GCP evidence directories without overwriting them during no-live mock validation.

Retain traced no-live remediation guard provenance for the current script state with deterministic normalized mock reaper evidence.
Validate typed #731 lifecycle/card state after review recovery and follow-up remediation.
Doctor #731 lifecycle readiness after review recovery and follow-up remediation.
